analysis:
Only CHANGELOG.md is changed. The supplied units are the BASE text (lines 1-561 of the v0.10.5 candidate and v0.10.4 sections). The head text is not supplied. The patch excerpt is truncated: it renames the v0.10.5 candidate heading to v0.10.6 and adds roughly 800 lines of new release notes. The visible head lines describe two-Mac clusters over Thunderbolt 5/RDMA, a `cluster_runtime` registration block, platform-derived pair approvals and qualifications, and `darkbloom cluster local`.

No code, workflow or configuration change is visible, so I identify no concrete security regression from the supplied evidence. The prose itself raises threat-model questions for later review, which I cannot confirm from the changelog:
- New attack surface. The cluster feature adds a new trust boundary between two provider Macs, covering peer authentication, RDMA/Thunderbolt data exposure and per-pair key custody. A-001 prompts and A-003 keys are in scope, since hidden states and prompts cross between Macs. The canonical threat model (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011) does not obviously cover this. The actual cluster code is outside this batch.
- Registration. A `cluster_runtime` registration block is self-reported and must not be treated as authorization (T-052, T-054). The changelog says approvals are derived platform-side from release facts. Whether the coordinator verifies this cannot be checked here.
- Local API. `darkbloom cluster local` and `darkbloom start --local` are local unauthenticated or keyed surfaces (TB-003).
- Prefix cache (T-041). The v0.10.5 notes mention SSD checkpoint changes and cache TTL refresh behaviour. The notes say these keep TTL, budget and ownership decisions unchanged. The source diff is not in this batch.

The next pass should examine the actual cluster source files, peer-link encryption and authentication, and whether the threat model needs a new trust boundary for clusters. needs_deeper_review is set true for that reason.
